html:
In 1616 the Tibetan lama Ngawang Namgyal fled into the valleys south of the Himalaya and, over the next decades, made them one country, Bhutan. He took the title Zhabdrung, "at whose feet one submits".

He was a leader of the Drukpa school of Tibetan Buddhism. A dispute over who was the true rebirth of a great Drukpa lama set him against the ruler of Tsang in Tibet, and he left. In the south he won over or beat the local lords and turned back several Tibetan invasions.

He built the state on lasting lines:

  • Dzongs, great fortress monasteries that served as both seats of monks and seats of government. Simtokha came first in 1629, then Punakha.
  • A dual system, with a chief abbot for religion and a civil ruler, the Druk Desi, for government.
  • A written legal code.

When he died in 1651 his death was kept secret for about half a century, with officials claiming he was in retreat. The country still calls itself Druk Yul, land of the Drukpa, and sacred sites such as Paro Taktsang belong to the same tradition.
